text: Then Solomon said: "The LORD has said that he would dwell in thick darkness.
And I have built for you a lofty house, a place for you to dwell in forever."
Then the king turned and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while all the assembly of Israel stood.
He said: "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who with his own mouth spoke to my father David and with his own hand has fulfilled it, saying:

'From the day I brought my people out of the land of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel in which to build a house for my name to be there, and I chose no man to be ruler over my people Israel.
But I have chosen Jerusalem for my name to be there, and I have chosen David to be over my people Israel.'
Now it was in the heart of my father David to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
But the LORD said to my father David, 'Because it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart.
Nevertheless, you are not the one to build the house; your son, who will come from your own body, he shall build the house for my name.'

Now the LORD has kept the promise he made: I have succeeded my father David and taken my seat on the throne of Israel, just as the LORD promised, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
There I have placed the ark, which contains the covenant of the LORD that he made with the people of Israel."
Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands.

He had made a bronze platform five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high, and had set it in the middle of the court. He stood on it, knelt down before the whole assembly of Israel, spread out his hands toward heaven,
and said: "LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven or on earth, keeping covenant and showing steadfast love to your servants who walk before you with all their heart.
You have kept your promise to your servant, my father David; what you spoke with your mouth you have fulfilled with your hand this very day.

Now therefore, LORD, God of Israel, keep for your servant, my father David, what you promised him when you said, 'You shall never fail to have a man to sit before me on the throne of Israel, if only your sons guard their way and walk in my law as you have walked before me.'
And now, LORD, God of Israel, let your word that you spoke to your servant David be confirmed.
But will God really dwell with man on the earth? Look, the heavens and the highest heavens cannot contain you—how much less this house that I have built!
Yet turn toward the prayer of your servant and his plea for mercy, LORD my God; hear the cry and the prayer that your servant prays before you.
May your eyes be open toward this house day and night, toward the place where you said you would put your name, to hear the prayer that your servant prays toward this place.
Hear the pleas of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from heaven, the place where you dwell—hear and forgive.
If someone sins against his neighbor and is required to swear an oath, and he comes and swears before your altar in this house,
then hear from heaven and act. Judge your servants: condemn the guilty by bringing his conduct down on his own head, and vindicate the righteous by rewarding him according to his righteousness.
If your people Israel are defeated before an enemy because they have sinned against you, and they turn back and confess your name and pray and plead with you in this house,
then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land you gave to them and to their fathers.
If the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, and they pray toward this place and confess your name and turn from their sin because you have afflicted them,

then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel, teaching them the good way in which they should walk, and send rain on your land, which you gave to your people as an inheritance.
When famine or plague comes to the land, or blight or mildew, locusts or grasshoppers, or when their enemies besiege them in any of their cities—whatever disaster or disease may come—
and when any prayer or plea is made by any person or by all your people Israel, each one knowing his own affliction and pain, and spreading out his hands toward this house,

versions.text: and when a prayer or plea is made by anyone among all your people Israel, each knowing his own affliction and pain, and he spreads out his hands toward this house,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew distinguishes two parties: "any individual person" (כָל־הָאָדָם) and "all your people Israel" (כֹל עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל). The current rendering collapses them into one, losing the deliberate contrast between the individual and the whole nation.

text: then hear from heaven, the place where you dwell, and forgive. Deal with each person, whose heart you know, according to all his ways—for you alone know the hearts of all people.

versions.text: then hear from heaven, the place where you dwell, and forgive. Deal with each person according to all his ways, for you alone know the human heart.
versions.explanation: The clause אֲשֶׁר תֵּדַע אֶת־לְבָבוֹ ("whose heart you know") has been dropped, so the verse loses one of its two parallel statements about God's knowledge of the heart.

versions.text: then hear from heaven, the place where you dwell, and forgive. Deal with each person according to all his ways, since you know his heart—for you alone know the hearts of all people.
versions.explanation: אֲשֶׁר תֵּדַע אֶת־לְבָבוֹ is a relative clause describing the person ("whose heart you know"), not a causal clause. Rendering it with "since" creates two stacked causal statements ("since... for..."), which is slightly redundant and blurs the parallel. Restoring the relative force keeps both statements about God's knowledge intact and reads more cleanly aloud.

text: so that they may fear you and walk in your ways all the days they live in the land you gave to our fathers.

versions.text: Then they will fear you and walk in your ways all the days they live in the land you gave to our fathers.
versions.explanation: לְמַעַן introduces a purpose clause continuing the petition of the previous verse ("so that"), not a simple prediction. "Then they will fear you" turns the request into a statement of outcome; "so that they may fear you" preserves the intent while still reading smoothly aloud.

text: And as for the foreigner who does not belong to your people Israel but comes from a distant land because of your great name and your mighty hand and your outstretched arm—when he comes and prays toward this house,

then hear from heaven, the place where you dwell, and do whatever the foreigner asks of you, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you as your people Israel do, and may know that this house I have built bears your name.
When your people go out to war against their enemies, wherever you send them, and they pray to you toward this city that you have chosen and the house I have built for your name,
then hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause.
When they sin against you—for there is no one who does not sin—and you become angry with them and hand them over to an enemy who takes them captive to a land far or near,
and if they come to their senses in the land of their captivity and repent and plead with you there, saying, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly,'

and if they turn back to you with all their heart and all their soul in the land of their captivity where they were taken, and pray toward their land that you gave to their fathers, toward the city you have chosen and the house I have built for your name,
then hear from heaven, the place where you dwell, their prayer and their pleas, and uphold their cause; and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
Now, my God, let your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.
And now arise, LORD God, and come to your resting place, you and the ark of your might. May your priests, LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and may your faithful ones rejoice in what is good.

versions.text: And now arise, LORD God, and come to your resting place, you and the ark of your might. May your priests, LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and may your faithful ones rejoice in your goodness.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads simply "rejoice in the good" (בַּטּוֹב), with no possessive pronoun. "Your goodness" narrows the sense to God's attribute, whereas the phrase refers more broadly to the good that God bestows.

text: LORD God, do not reject your anointed one. Remember your steadfast love for David your servant."

versions.text: LORD God, do not turn away the face of your anointed one. Remember your steadfast love for David your servant."
versions.explanation: "Turn away the face of" is a Hebrew idiom meaning to refuse or reject a petitioner; the literal rendering may confuse hearers in oral reading. (A footnote noting that the Hebrew is plural, "your anointed ones," could also be helpful.)
